summary: AstroVital is a mobile app and web dashboard that helps monitor an astronaut's health during long-duration space missions. It displays vital signs such as heart rate, oxygen, temperature, sleep and stress, and raises alerts when values suggest a possible anomaly. An interactive 3D body highlights the zones that need attention, so users can understand their status at a glance. The app connects to NASA's open API for space-weather data (DONKI), showing recent solar flares and radiation references, and lists every data source it uses. Vital signs are simulated for demonstration, since real astronaut data is not public. It matters because crews far from Earth face communication delays and limited medical support, and a clear, easy-to-read tool can help them recognize risks early and make safer decisions.
details:
The project consists of a mobile application and a website designed to monitor a user’s vital signs—such as their pulse—and display alerts whenever potential anomalies are detected. Data, retrieved via an API provided by the institution, is presented on a dashboard that includes a 3D model highlighting areas of concern.

The proposal aims to allow individuals to check their health status during a mission and receive notifications, enabling them to take action in response to potential risks. This tool is intended to help prevent incidents related to health issues. A planned future enhancement involves the integration of a wearable wristband for measuring vital signs.

Development of the project utilized a range of tools and technologies, including Android Studio, Visual Studio Code, SketchUp, GitHub Desktop, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, JSON, Kotlin, Java, and XML, alongside institutional APIs. The design prioritized a user-friendly visual interface, featuring navigation buttons, a history log, and account verification. The five-member team divided the tasks and subsequently integrated their individual contributions, taking into account the available timeframe, the feasibility of the wristband, and the implementation of the 3D model.
